newsitem.title: UK: Williams expects UK to clear Chubb bid.
newsitem.headline: Williams expects UK to clear Chubb bid.

text.p: Williams Holdings Plc said on Friday its 1.3 billion stg bid for fellow lockmaker Chubb Security Plc should not face any problems with Britain's competition authorities.

The deal is conditional on the Secretary of State for Trade and Industry indicating "in terms satisfactory to Williams" that the deal would not be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission for investigation.

But Williams said that the two businesses were largely complementary. "Williams does not anticipate that such a reference will be made and will be entering into discussions with the appropriate authorities to address any concerns that may arise," the firm said in a statement.

It said its Yale product range had particular strengths in door closers, panic exit devices, building locks and hotel systems, whilst Chubb's strengths were mortice and cylinder locks for residential and commercial markets.

Yale was focused on the provision of security "hardware," while Chubb's security interests embraced intruder detection, sophisticated access control and closed circuit TV systems, monitoring services and manned guarding, Williams said.
